# Independent ISO CAN FD wire vectors

`canfd_iso_wire_vectors.json` contains 128 complete, successfully acknowledged
frames, generated by Pierre Molinaro's independently authored CAN FD Saleae
simulator. They are **ISO**, with the upstream constructor explicitly set to
`CANFD_ISO_PROTOCOL`. No simulator implementation or calculated expected value
from DIR-Simulator is used to create them.

Reference implementation:

- Repository: https://github.com/pierremolinaro/canfd-plugin-for-saleae-logic-analyzer
- Commit: `e74bb6b49885bb27f8741849553e73fefcefb11a`
- File: `src/CANFDMolinaroSimulationDataGenerator.cpp`
- Source SHA-256: `9da38614ddef670437c6fe59f91fe0d3876f186e012cf06f19981a186ce6ddd6`
- Fixture SHA-256: `cf1b00b9ceb9e429e49d7ba5d680b8be3828de2080e0737898bb23ecdc90673e`

The generator script extracts the original `CANFDFrameBitsGenerator` class and
methods unchanged, supplies only its enum declarations and a C++ main function,
and compiles it with `g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -Wextra -O2`. The reference source
hash is enforced before extraction. Upstream's three-bit intermission is removed
from the emitted stream; the fixture covers SOF through the seventh EOF bit.
The CRC and dynamic stuff count come directly from upstream accessors. Nominal
and data phase counts come from upstream's per-bit rate flags. A BRS bit and CRC
delimiter together occupy exactly one nominal and one data bit, although each
individually switches rate at its sample point.

Coverage: all 16 DLC values, base and extended identifiers, zero and maximum
identifiers, alternating and mixed identifiers, and zero/all-one/alternating/mixed
payloads. The four patterns use respectively `(BRS, ESI)` values `(0,0)`, `(1,0)`,
`(0,1)`, `(1,1)`. CRC17 and CRC21 are exercised, including 16/20-byte boundary,
zero-byte frames, 64-byte frames, and stuff counts wrapping modulo eight.

Reproduce without invoking DIR-Simulator:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/pierremolinaro/canfd-plugin-for-saleae-logic-analyzer.git /tmp/canfd-reference
git -C /tmp/canfd-reference checkout e74bb6b49885bb27f8741849553e73fefcefb11a
python3 crates/dir-simulator/tests/fixtures/generate_canfd_iso_wire_vectors.py \
  --reference /tmp/canfd-reference --output /tmp/canfd-reproduced.json
cmp crates/dir-simulator/tests/fixtures/canfd_iso_wire_vectors.json /tmp/canfd-reproduced.json
```

Protocol target and primary sources:

- [ISO 11898-1:2015, edition 2, December 2015](https://www.iso.org/standard/63648.html).
  The codec targets this edition's CAN FD frame format. This edition has been
  superseded by ISO 11898-1:2024; no claim of complete 2024 conformance is made.
- [Arthur Mutter, Bosch, CAN Newsletter 1/2015](https://www.can-cia.org/fileadmin/cia/documents/publications/cnlm/previous_issues/15-1_cnlm.pdf),
  pages 6–10: ISO changes, Gray-coded dynamic stuff count with even parity,
  fixed stuff-bit placement and CRC initialization with only the MSB set.
- [CiA, CRC in CAN frames](https://www.can-cia.org/can-knowledge/cyclic-redundancy-check-crc-in-can-frames):
  CRC17/CRC21, dynamic stuff-bit coverage and the ISO/non-ISO distinction.
- [CiA, CAN FD](https://www.can-cia.org/can-knowledge/can-fd-the-basic-idea):
  BRS sample-point switching and field structure.
- [Pinned reference source](https://github.com/pierremolinaro/canfd-plugin-for-saleae-logic-analyzer/blob/e74bb6b49885bb27f8741849553e73fefcefb11a/src/CANFDMolinaroSimulationDataGenerator.cpp),
  including ISO CRC inputs and its BRS/CRC-delimiter sample-point timing.

The publicly accessible primary explanations and independent source provide
the algorithm evidence. A licensed full normative standard and ISO 16845
conformance suite were not available for this work. These vectors verify
ideal frame encoding, not controller conformance, electrical behavior,
retransmission, error confinement, or arbitrary captured-frame decoding.

Upstream code is not vendored. The reproduction script copies the upstream MIT
notice into its temporary generated C++ source. Reference author attribution:
Copyright (c) 2020 Pierre Molinaro, MIT License.
